claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
The initial FeCoNi material has an intrinsic coercivity of roughly 100 Oe.
The low coercivity of the initial FeCoNi material is caused by its high crystallographic symmetry.
Controlled cold rolling followed by stress-relief annealing can introduce a slight tetragonal distortion into an originally cubic fcc FeCoNi lattice.
The treatment leaves the material predominantly fcc while locally breaking cubic symmetry.
The induced tetragonal distortion increases magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The induced distortion enhances domain-wall pinning.
Increased anisotropy and domain-wall pinning make magnetic-domain reorientation more energetically costly.
The increased energetic cost of domain reorientation raises the coercive field.
The thermomechanical treatment will raise coercivity above 100 Oe relative to an untreated single-phase fcc control.
The thermomechanical treatment will produce only a minimal reduction in saturation magnetization.
The proposed effect applies to FeCoNi-based single-phase fcc alloys without major compositional modification.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase depends on the distortion, rolling strain, and annealing parameters.
Room-temperature vibrating-sample magnetometry can measure the treatment-induced changes in coercivity and saturation magnetization.

contradictions.description: The conditions describe processing as ambient, while the intervention explicitly requires an annealing treatment, which ordinarily entails elevated-temperature processing. No annealing temperature is given to resolve this inconsistency.
